metadata.name: anqa_core
metadata.description: Anqa — a perp DEX whose order book lives inside a Private Ephemeral Rollup

instructions.name: activate_asset
docs: Activate one more asset in an existing group — cross-margin markets
after the first, each priced by its own oracle.

accounts.name: venue_clock
docs: The venue's own clock. Bound to this group by seeds: the kernel trusts
whatever slot it is handed, so a caller-supplied account here would be
a way to stall or force accrual. See `state/venue_clock.rs`.

instructions.name: add_collateral
docs: Commit free equity behind this market's open position, moving its
liquidation price away without touching the position itself.

accounts.name: trader
docs: The portfolio owner, or a session key the owner granted.

accounts.name: session
docs: Present when a session key signs for the owner. Checked in the handler
via `trade_authorized`, like `place_order`.

accounts.name: oracle_state
docs: Read for `remove_collateral`'s margin check; never written. Removal
prices the position at the same guarded mark liquidation uses.

instructions.name: adl
docs: Auto-deleverage a profitable position — layer 4, reached only when
counterparty collateral, insurance and the haircut have all failed.
Permissionless, bounded by the kernel, and always emits an event.

accounts.name: keeper
docs: Permissionless.

accounts.name: portfolio
docs: The profitable account being deleveraged.

instructions.name: authorize_withdraw
docs: Rollup: let the risk engine judge the request, write the verdict into
the receipt, and send it home with the settle queued behind it.

accounts.name: payer
docs: Permissionless — this can only execute the owner's own signed request,
against the owner's own portfolio, into the owner's own receipt. A keeper
must be able to re-drive it if the validator-dispatched run failed.

accounts.name: portfolio
docs: The portfolio. Bound to the receipt's owner in the handler, since the
owner is only known once the receipt is deserialized.

accounts.name: receipt
docs: on base layer it is owned by the delegation program, so Anchor's typed
owner check cannot be used across both layers.

instructions.name: cancel_all_orders
docs: Pull every resting order this trader has. The panic button — permitted
even while the market is paused, since a pause must not trap orders.

accounts.name: session
docs: Present when a session key signs for the owner; judged in the handler.

instructions.name: cancel_order
docs: Rollup: cancel one of your resting orders.

accounts.name: trader
docs: The portfolio owner, or a session key the owner granted.

accounts.name: session
docs: Present when a session key signs for the owner; judged in the handler.

accounts.name: book
docs: Zero-copy; see `state::book`.

instructions.name: cancel_trigger_order
docs: Disarm a trigger slot.

accounts.name: session
docs: Present when a session key signs for the owner; judged in the handler.

instructions.name: cancel_up_to
docs: Pull only quotes at or more aggressive than a price, leaving the passive
remainder working. The everyday risk tool for a maker.

accounts.name: session
docs: Present when a session key signs for the owner; judged in the handler.

instructions.name: checkpoint_portfolio
docs: Rollup: permissionless portfolio checkpoint to base — a commit is a
truthful snapshot and can only help the owner. Keeper slow tick.

instructions.name: claim_deposit
docs: Credit a portfolio with deposits recorded on the base-layer ledger.
Runs wherever the portfolio lives; idempotent via its high-water mark.

accounts.name: caller
docs: Permissionless — crediting a trader their own deposit can only help them.

accounts.name: portfolio
docs: The portfolio. Delegated to the rollup when this runs there.

accounts.name: ledger
docs: Base-layer ledger. **Read only** — the rollup cannot write it, which is
exactly why the high-water mark lives in the portfolio instead.

accounts.name: receipt
docs: Deserialized and PDA-verified by hand; committed home with the close
queued behind it.

instructions.name: close_deposit_receipt
docs: Base layer: close a landed deposit receipt, rent back to the trader.
Signerless — dispatched by the validator, retryable by anyone.

accounts.name: receipt
docs: Deserializable as ours again only once the rollup has undelegated it.

instructions.name: close_position
docs: Close an open position, reduce-only by construction.
Sized to the position the kernel actually holds, so a close can never
overshoot into an opposite position. IOC — a close that silently rests
is a position you believe you exited and have not.

accounts.name: trader
docs: The portfolio owner, or a session key the owner granted.

accounts.name: session
docs: Present when a session key signs for the owner; judged in the handler.

instructions.name: collect_fees
docs: Collect accrued protocol revenue. Cannot reach collateral or insurance.

instructions.name: commit_and_undelegate_book
docs: Rollup: commit and return the book to base chain.

accounts.name: book
docs: Zero-copy; see `state::book`.

instructions.name: commit_asset_slots
docs: Rollup: checkpoint the slabs to base, keeping the rollup.

instructions.name: commit_book
docs: Rollup: checkpoint book state to base chain.

accounts.name: book
docs: Zero-copy; see `state::book`.

instructions.name: commit_portfolio
docs: Checkpoint the portfolio to base layer without leaving the rollup.

instructions.name: commit_risk_group
docs: Rollup: checkpoint the risk group to base, keeping the rollup. The
keeper's slow tick — bounds what an unplanned undelegation can lose.

instructions.name: crank
docs: Advance mark price and funding for an asset. The mark is read from Pyth;
the caller cannot supply a price.

accounts.name: cranker
docs: Permissionless — anyone may advance the market. They supply no prices,
only the transaction.

accounts.name: internal_oracle
docs: The relayed price. Delegated into the rollup alongside the book, which is
the only way this instruction can read a price there at all.

accounts.name: venue_clock
docs: The venue's own clock. Bound to this group by seeds: the kernel trusts
whatever slot it is handed, so a caller-supplied account here would be
a way to stall or force accrual. See `state/venue_clock.rs`.

instructions.name: create_book_permission
docs: Base layer, admin: permission the book — on a TEE validator only the
listed members (the engine) can read it. The program signs for the
book PDA.

accounts.name: permission
docs: permission program.

instructions.name: create_portfolio_permission
docs: Base layer, trader: permission your portfolio — on a TEE validator
only you and the members you list (the engine) can read it.

accounts.name: portfolio
docs: this program signs for it by those seeds.

accounts.name: permission
docs: permission program.

instructions.name: create_trader_orders_permission
docs: Base layer: record who may read a trader's order mirror. Must run
before delegation and before the rollup-side hide — the ephemeral
permission extends this record rather than creating one.

accounts.name: buffer_asset_slots
docs: payer once the delegation program has consumed the snapshot.

instructions.name: delegate_portfolio
docs: Move the portfolio into the rollup. Session-based: the trader chooses when
their state goes in and when it comes home.

accounts.name: portfolio
docs: this trader and market, so nobody can delegate somebody else's portfolio.

instructions.name: delegate_trader_orders
docs: Delegate a trader's order mirror into the rollup, beside the book it
projects.

instructions.name: delegate_venue_clock
docs: Send the clock into the rollup with the risk group it belongs to.

instructions.name: deposit
docs: Base layer: deposit collateral. One of only two instructions that move
tokens. With `queue_claim` a deposit receipt is delegated to the rollup
with `claim_deposit` queued behind it, so deposit → credited is one
signature; the receipt then closes itself via `close_deposit_receipt`.

accounts.name: ledger
docs: Must already exist — see `initialize_ledger`. The ledger is a permanent
record, not something a deposit conjures into being.

accounts.name: trader_token_account
docs: Trader's USDC account.

accounts.name: vault
docs: Protocol custody. Holds every trader's collateral; never delegated to the
rollup, so collateral stays outside the enclave's trust boundary.

accounts.name: receipt
docs: handler when `queue_claim` is set; untouched otherwise.

instructions.name: fire_trigger_order
docs: Fire an armed trigger. Permissionless — a stop-loss is worthless if it
depends on its owner being online. Pair with `close_position` in the
same transaction.

accounts.name: keeper
docs: Permissionless keeper.

accounts.name: portfolio
docs: The owner's portfolio, which carries the trigger slots. The trigger
must not be consumable unless there is a position for it to act on.
The tag pins it to this market — isolated portfolios never cross.

instructions.name: forced_exit
docs: Base layer: settle a trader out against the last committed state of
their portfolio — the non-custodial escape hatch. Owner-signed always;
permissionless while the market is paused.

accounts.name: caller
docs: The owner, or — while the market is paused — anyone.

accounts.name: portfolio
docs: Must be program-owned, i.e. committed and undelegated — Anchor's owner
check is the whole "against last committed state" guarantee.

accounts.name: book
docs: the delegation program) the trader's resting orders died with the
rollup and only the reservation is cleaned up; if it is ours, the
orders are cancelled properly.

accounts.name: payout_to
docs: Where the money goes. Must belong to the portfolio's owner — a
permissionless exit can free someone's funds, never redirect them.

instructions.name: fund_insurance
docs: Fund an asset's insurance, long and short domains separately.
Permissionless — anyone may strengthen the backstop.

accounts.name: funder
docs: Permissionless. Anyone may strengthen the backstop; nobody can weaken it
here, because there is no withdrawal path in this instruction.

instructions.name: grant_session
docs: Owner grants (or renews) a browser-held session key: one wallet
signature, then popup-free trading until expiry.

accounts.name: session
docs: Platform-wide: one grant per owner, honoured by every market.

instructions.name: initialize_depth
docs: Base layer: create the book's public depth mirror.

instructions.name: initialize_insurance_vault
docs: Create the insurance vault — layer 2 of the loss waterfall, held apart
from custody so it cannot be paid out as trader collateral.

accounts.name: insurance_vault
docs: Its own authority, like the custody vault — no key can move it.

instructions.name: initialize_ledger
docs: Base layer: create the deposit ledger, empty. Must exist before any
deposit — it is the permanent record the rollup reads.

instructions.name: initialize_market
docs: Base layer: create a market and its empty book.

accounts.name: book
docs: Zero-copy: the book is far too large to deserialize onto the BPF stack.

instructions.name: initialize_protocol_vault
docs: Create the protocol vault — venue revenue, held apart from both trader
collateral and insurance.

accounts.name: protocol_vault_tokens
docs: Its own authority, like the other two vaults.

instructions.name: initialize_risk
docs: Base layer: stand up the risk engine for a market group.

accounts.name: asset_slots
docs: Pre-created and pre-sized by `prepare_asset_slots` — at `MAX_ASSETS`
slots the account exceeds the 10,240-byte CPI allocation limit, so it
cannot be `init`ed here. `zero` verifies it is program-owned and never
initialized; the seeds pin it to this group's PDA.

accounts.name: price_update
docs: The opening mark comes from Pyth too — not even the authority should be
able to seed a market at a price of its choosing.

instructions.name: initialize_tape
docs: Base layer: create the public fill tape — the one account in the dark
set the whole world may read.

instructions.name: initialize_trader_orders
docs: Base layer: create a trader's private mirror of their own resting
orders. The book is unreadable to them by design, so this is how a
trader sees what they left on it.

accounts.name: payer
docs: Whoever pays the rent. **Not** necessarily the owner: the engine
provisions these so a trader never has to sign for the privilege of
seeing their own orders.

accounts.name: owner
docs: field, never an authority — creating someone's mirror grants the
creator nothing, since the permission below names the owner and the
venue engine and the caller has no say in either.

instructions.name: initialize_vault
docs: Base layer: create the collateral vault. Never delegated to the rollup.

accounts.name: vault
docs: Its own authority — no human key can move collateral out of band.

instructions.name: initialize_venue_clock
docs: Move the depth mirror into the rollup, where the book it mirrors is.
Create the venue's own monotonic clock. Run on base, before delegation.

instructions.name: liquidate
docs: Liquidate an unhealthy account. Permissionless; refuses while healthy.

accounts.name: liquidator
docs: Permissionless — anyone may keep the book solvent.

accounts.name: portfolio
docs: The account under water.

instructions.name: liquidate_isolated
docs: Rollup: liquidate a position against its OWN collateral — isolated
margin's enforcement. Permissionless; refuses while the position's own
margin survives. The account-level `liquidate` is the backstop.

accounts.name: trader
docs: The portfolio owner, or a session key the owner granted.

accounts.name: session
docs: Present when a session key signs for the owner; judged in the handler.

instructions.name: modify_order
docs: Amend a resting order. Shrinking at the same price keeps queue
position; growing or repricing requeues, because both are new claims on
the book and time priority would otherwise be decorative.

instructions.name: open_portfolio
docs: Base layer: open a margin account. This is also the trader's seat.

instructions.name: place_multiple
docs: Post a ladder of post-only quotes in one transaction. All-or-nothing.

instructions.name: place_order
docs: Place an order. Crosses the resting book, then rests the remainder; every
fill is handed to the risk kernel, which may refuse it.
`hidden` withholds whatever rests from the published depth mirror. It
changes nothing else: the order keeps its price-time place in the same
queue, crosses on the same terms, and prints to the same public tape
when it fills. Dark markets only.
`remaining_accounts`: one `Portfolio` per maker this order may cross.

accounts.name: trader
docs: The portfolio owner, or a session key the owner granted.

accounts.name: session
docs: Present when a session key signs for the owner. Lives on base and is
clone-read in the rollup, like the market config. Checked in the
handler via `trade_authorized`.

accounts.name: book
docs: The order book. Delegated to the rollup in production.

accounts.name: oracle_state
docs: Last accepted mark plus the circuit breaker. Read, never written, here:
trading references the mark but must not be able to move it.

accounts.name: portfolio
docs: The taker's margin account. Bound to this market by its stored id;
ownership vs the signer is judged in the handler, because the signer
may be a session key rather than the owner the PDA is derived from.

instructions.name: place_trigger_order
docs: Arm a stop-loss or take-profit. Sits off-book, reserves no margin, and
is reduce-only when it fires.

accounts.name: session
docs: Present when a session key signs for the owner; judged in the handler.

instructions.name: prepare_asset_slots
docs: Base layer: create or grow the asset-slots account toward its full
size, one 10KB step per transaction. Must reach full size before
`initialize_risk` can run.

accounts.name: asset_slots
docs: then adopted by `initialize_risk` under its `zero` constraint.

instructions.name: prepare_asset_slots_buffer
docs: Base layer: create or grow the slabs' delegation buffer toward full
size, one 10KB step per transaction. Must reach full size before
`delegate_asset_slots` can run.

accounts.name: buffer_asset_slots
docs: transactions and consumed by `delegate_asset_slots`.

instructions.name: publish_depth
docs: Rollup: refresh the depth mirror from the book. Permissionless — it
publishes totals per price level and never who placed them.

accounts.name: caller
docs: Permissionless — a public total is nobody's secret.

instructions.name: publish_trader_orders
docs: Rollup: rebuild one trader's mirror from the book. Permissionless —
the seeds fix whose rows are copied, and the caller cannot read the
account they just wrote.

accounts.name: caller
docs: Permissionless: the projection is fixed by the account's own seeds,
and the caller cannot read what they publish.

instructions.name: realize_pnl
docs: Promote proven-backed profit from junior `pnl` into withdrawable
`capital`. Without this a winner can close a profitable position and
still be unabl
e to take the profit home. Permissionless.

accounts.name: caller
docs: Permissionless — anyone may promote anyone's proven profit.

instructions.name: reanchor_oracle
docs: Rollup, once per asset after delegation: jump the accrual clock into
the rollup's slot domain. Kernel-gated to empty markets, so it can
never skip funding or hide losses. Permissionless.

accounts.name: cranker
docs: Permissionless — the kernel's empty-market gate is the authority.

accounts.name: internal_oracle
docs: The relayed price — same trust path as the crank.

accounts.name: venue_clock
docs: The venue's own clock. Bound to this group by seeds: the kernel trusts
whatever slot it is handed, so a caller-supplied account here would be
a way to stall or force accrual. See `state/venue_clock.rs`.

instructions.name: refresh_portfolio
docs: Settle one account against the latest accrual.

instructions.name: remove_collateral
docs: Take excess collateral back out from behind this market's position;
what remains must still clear initial margin at the live mark.

accounts.name: trader
docs: The portfolio owner, or a session key the owner granted.

accounts.name: session
docs: Present when a session key signs for the owner. Checked in the handler
via `trade_authorized`, like `place_order`.

accounts.name: oracle_state
docs: Read for `remove_collateral`'s margin check; never written. Removal
prices the position at the same guarded mark liquidation uses.

instructions.name: request_withdraw
docs: Base layer: reserve collateral, open a withdrawal receipt, and delegate
it to the rollup. With `queue_authorize` the validator dispatches the
rollup leg itself; without it a keeper (or the client) drives it.

accounts.name: payout_to
docs: Where the payout will go. Captured now, while the trader is signing, so
the later signerless settle cannot be pointed anywhere else.

accounts.name: receipt
docs: exit, which is after the delegation CPI would need the bytes in place),
then delegated to the rollup. Seeds bind it to this trader and market.

instructions.name: revoke_session
docs: Owner kills the grant early. Base-layer, so it never depends on the
session key's cooperation.

instructions.name: set_book_private
docs: Rollup: make the book unreadable from outside. This is the
instruction that actually creates the dark book — see `set_private`.

accounts.name: book
docs: sign, which this program does by seeds.

instructions.name: set_dark
docs: Base layer, admin: flip a market between lit and dark matching.

accounts.name: book
docs: delegation program on base) when this flips; only its pending-queue
bytes are inspected, nothing is written.

instructions.name: set_portfolio_private
docs: Rollup: hide a trader's own position, entry and liquidation price.

accounts.name: portfolio
docs: can hide — or expose — somebody else's position.

instructions.name: set_trader_orders_private
docs: Hide a trader's order mirror from everyone but its owner. Without this
the mirrors would collectively undo the dark book.
Permissionless: the member list is fixed by the program to the owner
and the venue engine, so a caller gains nothing by driving it — which
is what lets the engine provision mirrors without a trader signature.

accounts.name: orders
docs: mirror that already belongs to the owner they named.

instructions.name: settle_fill
docs: Rollup: settle the oldest pending fill on a dark market through the
risk kernel and print it to the public tape. Strictly FIFO; driven by
the engine keeper, callable by anyone.

accounts.name: caller
docs: The engine keeper in practice; anyone in principle.

accounts.name: taker_portfolio
docs: The head fill's taker. Verified against the queue in the handler; the
tag pins it to THIS market's portfolio — isolated margin means a fill
may only ever draw on the collateral locked behind this market.

accounts.name: maker_portfolio
docs: The head fill's maker. Never the taker's account — self-trade
prevention cancels self-crosses at match time, so a self pending fill
cannot exist.

accounts.name: tape
docs: The public tape — the only account in the dark set the world reads.

instructions.name: settle_withdraw
docs: Base layer: pay out a settled receipt and release the reservation.
Signerless — dispatched by the validator, retryable by anyone.

accounts.name: receipt
docs: Deserializable as ours again only once the rollup has undelegated it —
which is exactly what makes a premature settle impossible.

accounts.name: payout_to
docs: The destination the trader signed for at request time. No signer here
can redirect it.

instructions.name: sweep_backing
docs: Expire a lapsed source-backing bucket. Permissionless maintenance:
without it, one expired bucket wedges every refresh in its domain.

accounts.name: caller
docs: Anyone; the keeper in practice.

accounts.name: venue_clock
docs: The venue's own clock. Bound to this group by seeds: the kernel trusts
whatever slot it is handed, so a caller-supplied account here would be
a way to stall or force accrual. See `state/venue_clock.rs`.

instructions.name: sync_internal_oracle
docs: Relay a verified Pyth price into the internal oracle account, so the
venue can still read a price once the book lives inside the rollup.
Permissionless — the keeper copies a verified number, it supplies none.

accounts.name: keeper
docs: Permissionless. Pays rent-exempt top-up only if the account is new.

accounts.name: price_update
docs: The real thing, read on base layer where its signature still means
something.

instructions.name: undelegate_asset_slots
docs: Rollup: commit the slabs and return them to base — the second half of
bringing the risk engine home for base-layer maintenance
(`fund_insurance`) or escape.

instructions.name: undelegate_portfolio
docs: Commit and return the portfolio to base layer.

instructions.name: undelegate_risk_group
docs: Rollup: commit the risk group and return it to base. Run this before
`undelegate_asset_slots`; see the module doc for why they're separate.

instructions.name: withdraw
docs: Base layer: withdraw collateral. Requires a flat account — the kernel
will not release funds out from under an open position.

types.name: AssetSlots
docs: Per-asset engine state for every market in the group.
The kernel's view constructor takes a contiguous `&mut [Market<T>]`, so all
assets live in **one** account rather than one account per asset. Each is an
isolated source domain, which is what bounds a blowup in one market to that
market.

fields.name: seq
docs: Monotonic arrival counter — the "time" in price-time priority.

fields.name: pending
docs: FIFO ring of matched-but-unsettled fills (dark markets only).

types.name: BookDepth
docs: The public face of a dark book.

fields.name: seq
docs: Bumped on every rebuild, so a client can tell a stale read from a
quiet market.

fields.name: bids
docs: Best-first: `bids[0]` is the highest bid, `asks[0]` the lowest ask.

fields.name: total_bid_lots
docs: Every *displayed* lot, including whatever sits past the published
levels. Hidden orders are excluded here as well as from the ladder, so
this is the venue's visible size, not its true one.

fields.name: bid_levels
docs: Levels actually populated on each side.

fields.name: _pad
docs: Explicit tail padding — `Pod` refuses a type the compiler had to pad.

types.name: BookSide
docs: One side of the book: the arena plus its two list heads.

fields.name: head
docs: Best order, or NIL when empty.

fields.name: free_head
docs: First free slot, or NIL when full.

types.name: DepositReceipt
docs: A deposit crossing into the rollup. Created **and delegated** on base by
`deposit`, carrying the queued `claim_deposit` the validator runs inside
the rollup; consumed on base by `close_deposit_receipt` once the credit
has landed.
The receipt is the *vehicle*, not the accounting: the credit itself is
still computed from the monotonic ledger against the portfolio's
high-water mark, so a lost or replayed receipt can never mint or lose a
deposit — at worst it costs the rent until someone closes it.

fields.name: amount
docs: What this deposit paid in, for the tape; the credit is ledger-derived.

fields.name: credited
docs: Set by the rollup once the portfolio was credited.

fields.name: base_lots
docs: Total base lots resting at this price, across every order.

types.name: Fill
docs: The only event that carries market information.

fields.name: count
docs: Total prints ever. `head` is `count % TAPE_ENTRIES`, so a reader can
detect how far behind it is and page accordingly.

fields.name: feed_id
docs: Feed this mirrors. Checked against the market's own on every read.

fields.name: price
docs: Price as published, still carrying its own exponent.

fields.name: conf
docs: Confidence interval, at the same exponent as `price`.

fields.name: ema
docs: Exponentially weighted price, for funding.

fields.name: publish_time
docs: Publish time reported by the oracle, not the time we relayed it.

fields.name: synced_at_slot
docs: Base-layer slot at which this relay was written.

fields.name: last_keeper
docs: Who last wrote it. Diagnostics only; the write path is permissionless.

types.name: Market
docs: Market configuration.
**Never delegated.** `place_order` reads this for tick size, fees, oracle
policy and the paused flag; inside the rollup it arrives as a read-only
clone of the base account (verified live on devnet). Keeping it on base is
load-bearing: delegation would flip its owner to the delegation program and
break every base instruction that reads `market` through Anchor's owner
check — `deposit`, the withdraw legs, `forced_exit`.
Consequence: admin writes (pause, oracle params) always happen on base, and
the rollup sees them on its next clone refresh.

fields.name: market_id
docs: Stable identifier, also the PDA seed.

fields.name: group_id
docs: The margin hub this market settles against. Every market in a group
shares one vault, one risk engine and one portfolio per trader —
cross-margin. Group-scoped PDAs are seeded by this, not `market_id`.

fields.name: authority
docs: Admin authority (multisig in production).

fields.name: tick_size
docs: Price increment, quoted in quote atoms per base lot.

fields.name: base_lot_size
docs: Base units per lot — the minimum tradable increment.

fields.name: base_decimals
docs: Decimals of the base asset, for client display.

fields.name: quote_decimals
docs: Decimals of the collateral/quote mint (6 for USDC). The mark price is
denominated in quote atoms, so this — not `base_decimals` — is what the
oracle read rescales to.

fields.name: taker_fee_bps
docs: Taker fee charged on notional, in basis points.

fields.name: maker_rebate_bps
docs: Maker rebate on notional, in basis points.

fields.name: paused
docs: Halts new orders while set; cancels remain allowed.

fields.name: dark
docs: Dark mode: the book account is private. Two things follow, and both are
consequences of the same fact rather than separate policies.
1. Fills settle through the pending queue (`settle_fill`) instead of
inline — a taker who cannot read the book cannot name the makers it
crosses, so crossing and crediting decouple.
2. Orders may be placed `hidden`, i.e. withheld from the published depth
mirror. Only meaningful here: where the book is readable, so is every
order in it, and the flag would conceal nothing.
Flipped by `set_dark` on base.

fields.name: asset_index
docs: Index of this market's asset inside the risk group's slot array.

fields.name: oracle
docs: Oracle policy. Fixed at creation; changeable only through a timelocked
admin path, because it governs this market's own liquidations.

fields.name: oracle_kind
docs: Which oracle backend this market reads.

types.name: OracleKind
docs: Where a market's price comes from.

types.name: OracleParams
docs: Per-market oracle policy. Fixed at market creation — a market must not be
able to loosen the rules that govern its own liquidations.

fields.name: feed_id
docs: Pyth feed id this market marks against.

fields.name: secondary_feed_id
docs: Optional second feed. Zero means single-source.

fields.name: max_age_secs
docs: Refuse prices older than this many seconds.

fields.name: max_conf_bps
docs: Refuse when Pyth's confidence interval exceeds this fraction of price.

fields.name: max_deviation_bps
docs: Refuse when two sources disagree by more than this.

fields.name: max_move_bps_per_interval
docs: Trip the breaker when the mark jumps more than this since the last
accepted price. Zero disables the band (first mark, or synthetics).

fields.name: freeze_slots
docs: Slots to stay frozen after the breaker trips.

fields.name: ema_weight_bps
docs: EMA smoothing, in basis points of the new sample (2000 = 20% new).

fields.name: max_band_bps
docs: **Execution band.** Orders and fills must be within this fraction of the
mark. This is the difference between a spot CLOB and a perp CLOB: on a
spot venue an off-market trade only means you sold cheap with your own
tokens, but on a perp venue it mints a position at that entry and the
mark instantly revalues it — creating value from nothing at the vault's
expense. Two accounts trading at price 1 while the mark is 65,000 would
hand one side enormous profit and bankrupt the other into insurance.
The risk kernel deliberately does not check this (it only rejects zero
and absurd prices); bounding execution against the oracle is the
wrapper's job.

fields.name: max_mark_staleness_slots
docs: Refuse to trade if the mark has not been cranked within this many slots.
If the crank stops, trading halts — the correct failure mode.

types.name: OracleState
docs: Live oracle state for a market: last accepted mark, the EMA funding is
computed against, and the circuit breaker.

fields.name: last_price
docs: Last accepted mark, in quote atoms.

fields.name: ema_price
docs: Exponentially weighted mark. Funding uses this, never a spot tick.

fields.name: frozen_until_slot
docs: While `slot < frozen_until_slot`, liquidations and leverage increases are
refused. Set when the move band or cross-source deviation trips.

fields.name: breaker_trips
docs: Diagnostics: how many times the breaker has tripped.

types.name: OrderAccepted
docs: Emitted on order placement. Carries no price, size, side, or owner — it exists
so integrators can confirm their own submission landed, correlated by the
client-supplied nonce they already know.

types.name: OrderCancelled
docs: Emitted on cancellation. Same reasoning as above.

types.name: PendingFill
docs: A fill that has matched on the book but not yet settled through the risk
kernel. Only exists on a **dark** market: the taker cannot name makers it
cannot see, so crossing and settling decouple — the book matches, the
queue records, and `settle_fill` (driven by the engine, which can see the
book) executes each pair through the kernel.

fields.name: taker_is_ask
docs: 0 = taker bought (taker takes the long leg), 1 = taker sold.

fields.name: maker_order_closed
docs: 1 when the match fully consumed the maker's resting order.

fields.name: reduce_only
docs: 1 when this fill came from `close_position` and must never increase or
reverse the taker's exposure when it eventually settles.

types.name: PermissionMember
docs: A permission-list entry, IDL-friendly. `flags` bits: 1 authority, 2 tx
logs, 4 tx balances, 8 tx messages, 16 account signatures. Read access to
the account itself comes with membership.

types.name: PermissionMemberArg
docs: A reader of a private account, and what they may see.

fields.name: flags
docs: Bitmask over the SDK's observability flags (authority, logs,
balances, message, signatures).

types.name: Portfolio
docs: A trader's margin account: collateral, positions, PnL, funding counters.
Large (9,291 bytes of kernel state), and deliberately so — it is bounded
storage the kernel can walk without ever scanning a global table, which is
what keeps margin checks and liquidation cranks compute-bounded and, later,
feasible inside an enclave.

fields.name: owner
docs: Anqa-side owner check, independent of the kernel's provenance header.

fields.name: market_id
docs: Market group id, little-endian (a `u64` here would force 8-byte
alignment and introduce padding, which `bytemuck::Pod` rejects).

fields.name: reserved_margin
docs: Initial margin reserved by this trader's **resting orders**, in quote
atoms, little-endian u128.
The kernel only knows about positions — an order that has not filled yet
is invisible to it. Without this, a trader could rest orders far beyond
what their collateral can support and only discover it at match time,
when the fill is refused and the book has already been walked. Anqa
therefore reserves margin at placement and releases it on cancel or fill.

fields.name: claimed_high_water
docs: How much of the base-layer ledger's `deposited` this portfolio has already
absorbed, little-endian u64.
The ledger only grows and the portfolio remembers where it got to, so
claiming credits exactly the difference. Replay is a no-op, and the
rollup never has to write anything on base layer to record that it
claimed — which it could not do anyway.

fields.name: asset_collateral
docs: Collateral the trader chose to stand behind each asset's position, in
quote atoms, little-endian u128 per asset slot.
The kernel pools capital at the account level — its legs carry size and
basis but no collateral of their own — so isolation per position has to
live here. This array is what makes "margin" on a position mean the
amount the trader put up rather than everything they hold, and what
`liquidate_isolated` measures a position's health against.
Set when a fill opens a position, added to when one grows, released in
full on close or isolated liquidation.

fields.name: asset_entry
docs: Size-weighted entry price for each asset's position, quote atoms per
lot, little-endian u128.
Isolated liquidation needs a position's *own* unrealised PnL, which
means its own entry. The kernel's leg carries a basis in its internal
accounting units; rather than reinterpret those, anqa records the
blended fill price as positions are built. Zeroed with the collateral
when the position closes.

fields.name: triggers
docs: Trigger orders (stop-loss / take-profit) ride **inside** the portfolio
so they delegate with it and fire inside the rollup, next to the book
they close into. As standalone base-layer accounts they became
unfireable the moment trading moved into the rollup: firing needs the
trigger, the oracle state, the portfolio and the book in one
transaction, and those lived on opposite sides of the boundary.

fields.name: feed_id
docs: `FeedId` but avoid the type alias because of compatibility issues with Anchor's `idl-build` feature.

fields.name: publish_time
docs: The timestamp of this price update in seconds

fields.name: prev_publish_time
docs: The timestamp of the previous price update. This field is intended to allow users to
identify the single unique price update for any moment in time:
for any time t, the unique update is the one such that prev_publish_time < t <= publish_time.
Note that there may not be such an update while we are migrating to the new message-sending logic,
as some price updates on pythnet may not be sent to other chains (because the message-sending
logic may not have triggered). We can solve this problem by making the message-sending mandatory
(which we can do once publishers have migrated over).
Additionally, this field may be equal to publish_time if the message is sent on a slot where
where the aggregation was unsuccesful. This problem will go away once all publishers have
migrated over to a recent version of pyth-agent.

types.name: PriceUpdateV2
docs: A price update account. This account is used by the Pyth Receiver program to store a verified price update from a Pyth price feed.
It contains:
- `write_authority`: The write authority for this account. This authority can close this account to reclaim rent or update the account to contain a different price update.
- `verification_level`: The [`VerificationLevel`] of this price update. This represents how many Wormhole guardian signatures have been verified for this price update.
- `price_message`: The actual price update.
- `posted_slot`: The slot at which this price update was posted.

fields.name: authority
docs: Who may collect. A multisig in production.

fields.name: token_account
docs: The token account holding the revenue.

fields.name: accrued
docs: Fees accrued and not yet collected, in quote atoms.

fields.name: lifetime_accrued
docs: Lifetime fees ever routed here.

fields.name: lifetime_collected
docs: Lifetime fees ever collected out.

fields.name: lifetime_to_insurance
docs: Lifetime fees diverted into insurance by the ratchet.

fields.name: insurance_target_bps
docs: Insurance target, as a fraction of open interest. While the fund sits
below this, every basis point of revenue is diverted to it.

fields.name: post_target_insurance_bps
docs: Share of revenue that keeps going to insurance once the target is met.
Zero means the treasury takes everything above target.

fields.name: hidden
docs: Withhold this rung from the published depth mirror. Per-quote rather
than per-batch, so a maker can show a ladder and hide size inside it —
the usual reason to want this at all.

types.name: RestingOrder
docs: One resting order. 72 bytes, 8-aligned, no implicit padding.

fields.name: next
docs: Next slot in whichever list this slot belongs to (live or free).

fields.name: active
docs: 1 when this slot holds a live order.

fields.name: hidden
docs: 1 when this order is withheld from the published depth mirror.
A hidden order is hidden and nothing else. It rests in this same arena,
in this same priority list, and crosses on exactly the same terms as a
displayed one — the flag is read only by `walk_prices`, which builds the
public ladder. Taken from the slot's own padding, so the struct is still
72 bytes and every account written before this field existed decodes
with `hidden == 0`.

types.name: RiskGroup
docs: Global risk state for a market group: config, insurance, vault totals, and
the solvency accounting shared across every asset in the group.

types.name: Side
docs: Side of the book. An instruction argument only — never stored in Pod state,
where it is a `u8`.

types.name: TapeEntry
docs: One print. 32 bytes.

types.name: TradeSession
docs: An owner's standing grant to one ephemeral key — **platform-wide**.
The grant names a trader, not a market: one signature arms one-click
trading across every market the owner holds an account on. Scope comes
from what the key may *do* (trade only), not from where.

fields.name: owner
docs: The portfolio owner who granted the session.

fields.name: market_id
docs: Unused since grants went platform-wide; kept for layout stability.

fields.name: session_key
docs: The ephemeral key allowed to sign trading instructions.

fields.name: expires_at
docs: Unix time after which the grant is dead. Re-grant to extend.

fields.name: seq
docs: Arrival sequence — the "time" in price-time priority. Lets a client
show queue position without reading anyone else's order.

fields.name: side
docs: 0 = bid, 1 = ask.

fields.name: hidden
docs: 1 when this order is withheld from the public depth ladder.

fields.name: seq
docs: Bumped on every rebuild, so a client can tell a stale read from a
trader who simply has nothing resting.

fields.name: published_at
docs: Unix time of the last rebuild, from the venue clock's host reading.
A row set that stopped updating is a keeper that stopped running, and
a trader should be able to tell that apart from an empty book.

fields.name: truncated
docs: 1 when the trader had more resting orders than `rows` can hold.

types.name: TriggerDirection
docs: Which way the mark must cross for the trigger to arm.

types.name: TriggerSlot
docs: A trigger order slot. Everything little-endian bytes so the containing
account stays `Pod` with no implicit padding.
Addressed by `trigger_id`, **never by slot index** — indices are storage,
ids are identity. (An index-addressed API plus slot reuse is a live
time-of-check races surface for permissionless keepers.)

fields.name: trigger_id
docs: Caller-supplied identity, unique among this portfolio's active slots.

fields.name: trigger_price
docs: Mark price, quote atoms, at which this arms.

fields.name: limit_price_in_ticks
docs: Worst acceptable execution price, in ticks — the slippage bound applied
when the trigger converts into a live close.

fields.name: max_base_lots
docs: Zero means "whatever the position is when it fires".

fields.name: armed_at_slot
docs: Slot at which this was armed. A trigger cannot fire in the slot it was
armed in — blocks atomic arm-then-fire extraction.

fields.name: asset_index
docs: Which asset in the group this protects.

fields.name: direction
docs: 0 = fire when mark rises to/above; 1 = fire when mark falls to/below.
Matches `TriggerDirection`'s variant order.

types.name: UserDepositLedger
docs: Per-trader, per-market, base layer. Never delegated.

fields.name: deposited
docs: Cumulative collateral ever paid into the vault. **Monotonic** — this is
what makes the high-water claim idempotent.

fields.name: withdrawn
docs: Cumulative collateral ever paid back out.

fields.name: reserved
docs: Currently committed to an in-flight withdrawal and not spendable.

types.name: VenueClock
docs: The venue's monotonic clock, one per risk group.
Travels with the risk group: delegated with it, committed with it,
undelegated with it. Separated from it only because `RiskGroup` is a fixed
byte image of the kernel header with no room to spare, and growing that
account would invalidate every venue already running.

fields.name: group_id
docs: Which risk group this clock belongs to.

fields.name: venue_slot
docs: What the kernel is told. Only ever increases.

fields.name: last_raw
docs: The last slot the host chain reported, in whatever frame it was using.
Meaningful only as the baseline for the next reading.

fields.name: frame_changes
docs: How many times the host's clock has been seen to move backwards —
operational visibility, since each one is a validator change or a
restart and is worth noticing.

types.name: VerificationLevel
docs: Pyth price updates are bridged to all blockchains via Wormhole.
Using the price updates on another chain requires verifying the signatures of the Wormhole guardians.
The usual process is to check the signatures for two thirds of the total number of guardians, but this can be cumbersome on Solana because of the transaction size limits,
so we also allow for partial verification.
This enum represents how much a price update has been verified:
- If `Full`, we have verified the signatures for two thirds of the current guardians.
- If `Partial`, only `num_signatures` guardian signatures have been checked.
# Warning
Using partially verified price updates is dangerous, as it lowers the threshold of guardians that need to collude to produce a malicious price update.

fields.name: authorized
docs: Zero means the kernel refused; the receipt still travels home so the
reservation can be released.

types.name: WithdrawReceipt
docs: The receipt itself. Created **and delegated** on base, authorized inside
the rollup, committed-and-undelegated back, consumed on base — the only way
a rollup decision can reach the vault.
Delegation is what makes the lifecycle race-free: while the request is in
flight the receipt is owned by the delegation program, so the base-layer
settle physically cannot run early. Only after the rollup hands it back —
with or without an authorization — does settling become possible.

fields.name: requested
docs: What the trader asked for and the ledger reserved.

fields.name: authorized
docs: What the risk kernel actually permitted. Meaningless until `Authorized`,
and zero if the kernel refused — a refusal still comes home as a
receipt, so the reservation can be released.

fields.name: payout_to
docs: Where the payout goes. Captured at request time, when the trader signed,
so the permissionless settle cannot be pointed anywhere else.

types.name: WithdrawStage
docs: Stages a withdrawal as it crosses the boundary.
